source.title: Exploit Where Optimizer Explores via Residuals
source.authors: An Xu; Zhou-Yuan Huo; Heng Huang

record.file_problem: The supplied full text is readable. Its running header and title say “Detached Error Feedback for Distributed SGD with Random Sparsification,” while the metadata title says “Exploit Where Optimizer Explores via Residuals”; the supplied document is the former.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports image-classification results on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet comparing a new distributed gradient-compression method with SGD and other methods, and reports test-accuracy changes over training. This is a new setting for the generalization claim, but it does not test memorization of random labels or the gap between train and test error as formulated in the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported test-accuracy outcomes for the studied methods and training stages. Although training loss is plotted and discussed, the text does not report paired training-error and test-error measurements that test the mapped versions. The text's discussion of prior work is not recorded as this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study compares gradient-compression algorithms and derives stability-based generalization bounds. None of its results tests V1–V8: compression ratio is not batch size or network width, DEF-A is not an adaptive optimizer, and no sharpness–gap correlation is measured. Reporting held-out accuracy in a new setting alone does not qualify as T3. The study also does not use a listed claim as a tool, so T4 does not apply.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that DEF(-A) improves over existing error-feedback variants with random block-wise sparsification, that DEF-A can attain higher test accuracy earlier than DEF and SGD, and that substantial compression can retain accuracy comparable to SGD. They also emphasize their convergence bounds and theoretical connection to SGD with iterate averaging.
record.recipe_differences: Studies detached error feedback and its accelerated variant for distributed SGD with random block-wise gradient sparsification, comparing them with existing compression methods and uncompressed SGD. It does not implement the original claim's random-label or generalization-gap tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression ratio changes final test accuracy; for DEF and DEF-A on VGG-16/CIFAR-10, λ choices also change accuracy. DEF-A's reported early test-accuracy advantage decreases as the learning rate becomes smaller.

fits_no_version.finding: DEF and DEF-A retain accuracy near uncompressed SGD under substantial gradient compression. At ratio 64, CIFAR-10 accuracies are 93.75% and 93.61% versus 93.76%; ImageNet accuracies are 76.16% and 76.37% versus 76.04%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detached error feedback can preserve held-out image-classification accuracy under random block-wise gradient sparsification.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 and Figure 3 report earlier test-accuracy gains for DEF-A over DEF at compression ratio 64, described as about 15% on CIFAR-10 and 25% on ImageNet before the first learning-rate decay; the advantage shrinks at smaller learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DEF-A can improve early-training held-out accuracy relative to DEF under the tested compression recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.6 and 4.10 derive improved stability-based generalization bounds for DEF-A and iterate averaging, alongside worse optimization-error bounds, under stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression or iterate averaging can improve theoretical generalization bounds through a trade-off with optimization error.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: The reported experiments evaluate test accuracy and training loss, not the paired training-error/test-error gap targeted by the claim versions. The early-training accuracy improvements are described in text without exact values in the supplied text; those curves are figure-only. Table 2 provides no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports additional CIFAR-10/100 test accuracies for VGG-16, ResNet-110 and WRN-28-10 across SGD, EF, SAEF, PSync, DEF and DEF-A; omitted to keep the extracted outcomes focused on the reported ratio sweeps and avoid exceeding the study’s relevance to the claim. Tables 1 and 2 include EF and SAEF/PSync comparator cells not extracted; they compare compression methods and do not measure a claim version. Table 4's λ sweep is summarized in method_sensitivity; it does not test a listed version.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or matched natural-label comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or manipulation of local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison or comparison of tuning budgets.
No batch-size sweep or test of recipes that recover large-batch performance; batch sizes are fixed within each workload.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, ranking of generalization gaps, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied title matches the supplied arXiv v3 text; the record reports a metadata-title discrepancy. All tabulated row values match the supplied text. The lack of paired training and test errors is not the general reason for exclusion: most listed versions require other specific interventions or comparisons, which this study does not perform.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
